title: Shimon of HaMitzpeh
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: (A Tanna in Temple times.) In Mishnah Peah 2:6: an incident in which Rabbi Shimon of HaMitzpeh sowed (two kinds of wheat), and came before Rabban Gamliel (the Elder); they went up to the Chamber of Hewn Stone and asked. Nachum the Scribe said: “I have received from Rabbi Meyasha,” etc.

In Yoma 14b: “Rav Huna said: Who taught Tamid? Rabbi Shimon of HaMitzpeh”; and it was taught on this, “Rabbi Shimon of HaMitzpeh differs concerning the daily offering,” etc. Rabbi Yochanan said: “Who taught the Order of the Day? Rabbi Shimon of HaMitzpeh.” In the Jerusalem Talmud there, 2:2: “Rabbi Yochanan said: Tamid is Rabbi Shimon of HaMitzpeh’s.” Hyman infers from the phrase “Rabbi Shimon of HaMitzpeh differs concerning the daily offering” some slight support for the possibility that he was a Kohen and served in the Temple.

notes.text: Saved Davidson Yoma14b fully writes Rav Huna. תמיד concerns the daily offering and the tractate/procedure discussion; Hyman’s slight support for priesthood remains expressly tentative, not a proven priestly identity.

The consulted Yoma 14b explicitly has Rav Huna, then the objection distinguishing Tamid from Shimon of HaMitzpeh’s daily-offering procedure, followed by Yochanan’s attribution of the Yoma order. Hyman’s slight inference of priesthood remains tentative; teaching a procedure is not independently treated as proof of priestly identity.
